reviewer: daily-training-brief (autonomous scheduled run, about 6 AM Vancouver time on this run)
brief:
Today, 28 October, is Legs A, and it is the third day of the deload week, which runs to 1 November. Nothing new has been logged since Pull A at Vancouver on 23 October: no session arrived for 24, 25, 26 or 27 October. If you trained and it has not synced, open the app so it uploads, because a session that is not in the log is not in this review. No review ran yesterday, 27 October: the scheduled run had been firing at about 5:30 in the evening Vancouver time and now fires at about 6 in the morning, and 27 October fell in the gap when it moved, so this one replaces it; nothing about the program has changed since version 4 on 26 October, and nothing changes today, because not one of the 26 October changes has been trained yet and there is no new evidence to revisit them on. This review repeats the 26 October one, and says so.

Two of the deload's seven days are gone with no session logged in it. Its job was to give every lift a number on this gym's machines before the assessment week starts on 2 November. Pull A already has its Vancouver numbers from 23 October; the other five sessions have none, and there are five days left, today and four more, so that is one session every day: Legs A tonight, then Push B, Pull B, Legs B, Push A. If one has to go, let it be Push A, because its chest press, pec deck and overhead triceps share machines with Push B, so Push B's numbers carry. If the week ends with nothing logged, the plan is simple: the assessment week, 2 to 8 November, becomes the week you find every machine at Vancouver, every lift opens at the deload starting points already on the cards, and the prep block gets programmed on 9 November from whatever those seven days log. The three decisions already dated 2 November (chest at 19 planned against a ceiling of 18, the calf press slot, the leg extension slot) stand.

Tonight, Legs A at Vancouver, deload numbers, the same as 26 October because the evidence is the same, all starting points on machines you have not used: leg press, feet low, 150 for 8, two sets. Bulgarian split squat, 15 lb dumbbells, 8 each leg, one set. Leg curl, 95 for 10, two sets. Leg extension, 120 for 12, one set. Adductor 60 for 12 and abductor 45 for 12, one set each, back to back. Calf press 230 for 12, two sets. Cable crunch 40 for 10, two sets. Twelve sets in all, every set stopping with four reps still in the tank. This review also carries deload starting numbers for the other five sessions, so that if you train on consecutive days before a new review lands, the card shows the number the review names; they drive the cards through 31 October, as long as nothing new has synced, and once a session syncs the next morning's review takes over. If a machine reads heavier or lighter than that, change the weight and log what you used; the point tonight is a clean, easy set on each machine, not a number. If the gym has no leg extension or no calf press, do the closest thing it has in that slot and mark it, because that is what decides whether those two slots stay after the deload.

Two things for you. This review landed at about 6 AM Vancouver time today, not a quarter to six in the evening as on 25 and 26 October, so you have it before you train. And no bodyweight has been logged since 23 August (207 lb); a morning weigh-in this week, before the assessment, would help. The show, 1 March, is 124 days away.

block.why: Nothing new has been logged since the 26 October review, and no review ran on 27 October: the scheduled run fired at about 5:30 in the evening Vancouver time on 25 and 26 October and at about 6 this morning, and 27 October fell in the gap when the slot moved (the run list shows no run between them, and there is no coach commit for that date); today's review replaces it. The last session that arrived is still Pull A at Vancouver on 23 October (deadlift 235 for 5, 5, 5; 18 of 19 sets in 46 minutes). Today, 28 October, is the third day of the one-week deload (26 October to 1 November): two of its seven days have passed with no session logged, and the next session is still Legs A. The assessment week is 2 to 8 November, prep starts 9 November, and the show is 124 days out. What the third build block (28 September to 25 October) did has not changed since it was written up on 26 October: 11 sessions across four gyms; the Push B shoulder press moved (22.5 kg for 10s on 12 October to 25 kg for 8 and 9 on 15 October), the deadlift came back from 225 (sick, 8 October) to 235 for 5s, and almost everything else re-found a machine each week; leg nights were the ones dropped (Legs B last ran 5 October, Legs A ran 11 of 20 sets on 14 October). The structural changes for this boundary were made on 26 October in program version 4 (shoulder press off Push A, dumbbell row and barbell RDL in for the smith lifts, Legs B press to feet low, ab wheel rollout in, two cable lateral raise sets and a fourth shrug set added) and none is revisited today: not one of them has been trained yet, so there is no evidence to revisit them on, and the reversal guard would refuse it anyway. Nothing changes today, by decision: a program altered twice in three days with zero sessions between the two edits would be the panel's old habit under a new name. What the deload is for is at risk: its job was one gym's numbers for every lift before the assessment on 2 November. Pull A has its Vancouver numbers (23 October); the other five sessions have none, and five days remain (today and four more), so that is one session every day in rotation order, Legs A, Push B, Pull B, Legs B, Push A, with Push A the one to drop if one must go, because its chest press, pec deck and overhead triceps share machines with Push B. Deload overrides are written for all six sessions on this packet so each card shows the number the review names; the packet drives cards through 31 October while nothing new has synced. If the week ends with nothing logged, the plan at the boundary is this: the assessment week (2 to 8 November) doubles as the finding week at Vancouver, every lift opens at the deload starting points already on the cards, and the prep block is programmed on 9 November from whatever those seven days log. The three decisions dated 2 November (chest, calves, leg extension) stand. Tonight's Legs A numbers are the same as on 26 October because the evidence is the same.

chest.why: Nineteen a week on paper, one over the ceiling of 18, and all 19 are direct sets (incline 4, two chest presses 6, two crossovers 6, dips 3). Left alone on 26 October and again today: the 8.8 a week actually done over four weeks is missed nights (Push A last ran 6 October; nothing 16 to 22 October), not a short plan, and the last chest nights were hard work on two different smith movements (smith incline bench 65, 70, 75 kg for 9, 8, 8 at Chennai on 15 October; flat smith 75 kg for 8, 8 on 12 October), which says the chest is being trained, not that a trend can be read across them. A build-block pass through the six days has taken 10 to 12 calendar days, so the real weekly chest dose is well under the ceiling. Re-read at the 2 November assessment, when the prep block is programmed; in deferred.

front-delts.why: Decided and acted on 26 October in program version 4; nothing has been logged since, so the verdict today is hold on the same evidence. Cut on 26 October: the Push A shoulder press is removed, taking direct front-delt sets from 11 a rotation (incline press 4, Push A press 3, Push B press 4) to 8, inside the direct range of 4 to 10. The Push A press had not gained a rep in its last three visits (45 lb for 9, 9, 9 on 8 and 19 September; 20 kg for 8, 8, 8 at Singapore on 6 October) while the Push B press moved (25 kg for 8 and 9 on 15 October), so the stalled one goes. The 15.5 on paper is those 8 plus half a set from each of the 15 chest-press, dip and crossover sets; that helper credit is why it still reads over the ceiling of 10, and it is not cut further.

side-delts.why: Decided and acted on 26 October in program version 4; nothing has been logged since, so the verdict today is hold on the same evidence. Raised on 26 October: 6 direct sets a rotation (Push A machine raise 3, never yet run because Push A last trained 6 October; Push B dumbbell raise 3) against a direct floor of 8, and 4.4 a week done over four weeks. The last real side-delt sets were 7.5 kg for 10, 10, 10 at Chennai on 12 October; on 15 October the slot was a bent-over cable raise, a rear-delt lift. Two sets of cable lateral raise go on the end of Pull A, making 8 direct (10 on paper with the Push B press's half credit). Not a fourth set on a push night, because on 23 August he wrote that four in one session seemed a lot.

rear-delts.why: Ten direct sets (reverse pec deck 3 and 3, face pulls 2 and 2), inside the direct range of 6 to 12; the 15.5 on paper adds half a set from each pulldown and row, which is why it reads over the ceiling, and no sets are cut for a helper count. Face pulls 22.5 lb for 14, 14 at Vancouver on 23 October; reverse pec deck 50 kg for 11s at Chennai on 12 October and skipped on 15 October. Hold.

lats.why: Decided and acted on 26 October in program version 4; nothing has been logged since, so the verdict today is hold on the same evidence. Seventeen direct sets (wide pulldown 3, seated row 4, the new chest-supported row 4, close pulldown 3, straight-arm 3), 18 on paper with the rollout's half credit, at the ceiling of 18. The rotation is the Pull B smith row becoming a chest-supported dumbbell row: a different smith machine every visit since September, so its number never settled. Wide pulldown 105, 110, 120 for 9, 9, 8 at Vancouver on 23 October; close pulldown 130 for 8, 8 at Chennai on 13 October. 8.3 done a week is missed nights, not the plan.

upper-back.why: Decided and acted on 26 October in program version 4; nothing has been logged since, so the verdict today is hold on the same evidence. Eight direct sets (seated row 4, and from 26 October the chest-supported dumbbell row 4 in place of the smith row), the floor of the direct range 8 to 16; the 19.5 on paper is half credit from every pulldown, deadlift, hinge and rear-delt set, which is why it reads over the ceiling, and nothing is cut for that. The seated row got all four sets at Vancouver on 23 October, 105 then 115 for 12, 12, 11, 10. The rotation is the smith row swap.

traps.why: Decided and acted on 26 October in program version 4; nothing has been logged since, so the verdict today is hold on the same evidence. Raised on 26 October: 3 direct sets (the shrug) against a direct floor of 4; the rest of the 9.5 on paper is half credit from the deadlift, face pulls and lateral raises. The shrug goes to four sets, because every shrug night since 3 September has had its top set at 15 or more (80 for 15, 15, 15 on 3 September; 35 kg for 15s on 15 September; 27.5 kg for 15, 15 at Warsaw on 23 September, a deload night; 36 kg for 15, 15, 13 at Singapore on 3 October; 55 kg reverse smith shrug for 16, 17, 18 at Chennai on 13 October), with one set under 15 in those five nights, the 13 on 3 October; 25 August itself was 80 for 12, 12, 12. 3.1 done a week because Pull B has not run since 13 October.

lower-back.why: No direct slot: the 3.5 on paper is half credit from the deadlift (4) and the new barbell RDL (3), which is under the direct floor of 2 by that reading. Held without a direct lift on purpose: a heavy deadlift and a barbell RDL in the same week already load the lower back isometrically on every rep, and a back extension on top of them is what a trainer adds when the hinges come out, not while they are in. Deadlift 235 for 5, 5, 5 at Vancouver on 23 October with no complaint logged. If he wants a direct lower-back lift anyway, it is one line to add.

biceps.why: Eleven direct sets (dumbbell curl 3, hammer 3, incline curl 2, reverse curl 3), inside the direct range of 8 to 14; the 18 on paper adds half a set from each pulldown and row, which is why it reads over the ceiling, and nothing is cut for that. At Vancouver on 23 October: dumbbell curl 30 lb for 8, 8, 8 and hammer curl 37.5 for 10, 10, 10, both at the bottom of their ranges on new equipment. Hold.

triceps.why: Eleven direct sets (overhead 3 and 3, reverse-grip pushdown 2, dips 3), inside the direct range of 8 to 14; the 19.5 on paper adds half a set from each of the four presses and the straight-arm pulldown, down from 21 after the Push A shoulder press came off, and that helper credit is why it reads over the ceiling. On 15 October the overhead slot was an overhead extension, 45 lb for 13, 15, the reverse-grip slot a rope pushdown, 70 kg for 12, 14, and the dips were skipped. Hold.

forearms.why: Six direct sets (hammer and reverse curls), inside the direct range of 2 to 8; the 12 on paper adds half a set from the dumbbell curl, the four shrug sets, the pushdown and the barbell RDL, which is why it reads over the ceiling, and nothing is cut for that. Hammer curl 37.5 for 10s at Vancouver on 23 October; reverse curl 99 for 12 at Chennai on 13 October. Hold.

quads.why: Decided and acted on 26 October in program version 4; nothing has been logged since, so the verdict today is hold on the same evidence. Raised on 26 October from 10 direct sets to 13: the Legs B leg press moves from feet high to feet low, so Legs B now has the smith squat and a quad-biased press. Quads were named the most under-served muscle on 13 October and have averaged 3.4 a week done; the last quad work was a smith squat in the leg-press slot at Chennai on 14 October (45 kg for 5, 7, 8) and split squats at 20 lb. The 25 October review said a Legs A at Vancouver would be the read for this; it did not happen, and the change rests on the set count alone. Now 13 direct against 13 direct hamstrings.

hamstrings.why: Decided and acted on 26 October in program version 4; nothing has been logged since, so the verdict today is hold on the same evidence. Cut on 26 October from 16 direct sets a rotation to 13: the Legs B feet-high leg press (hamstrings and glutes) becomes feet low (quads). What remains is the deadlift 4, the barbell RDL 3 and two leg curls 6, inside the direct range of 8 to 14; the 15.5 on paper adds half a set from the split squat and smith squat, which is why it still reads over the ceiling. 6 done a week because leg nights are the ones skipped; the only hamstring work since 5 October is the 23 October deadlift.

glutes.why: Twelve direct sets (deadlift 4, split squat 2, RDL 3, smith squat 3), inside the direct range of 6 to 14 after the feet-high press went; the 16 on paper adds half a set from two leg presses and the abductor, which is why it reads over the ceiling, and nothing is cut for that. Glute work since 5 October: the 14 October smith squat (45 kg for 5, 7, 8), split squats (20 lb for 8, 10) and kettlebell hip thrust at Chennai, and the 23 October deadlift. Hold.

adductors.why: Two direct sets on Legs A, the floor of the direct range 2 to 6; the 7.5 on paper adds half a set from the two leg presses, the smith squat and the split squat, which is why it reads over the ceiling, and nothing is cut for that. Not logged since 80 lb for 15, 15 at Singapore on 5 October; skipped at Chennai on 14 October. Tonight at Vancouver is the next read, if the gym has the machine.

abductors.why: Two planned, exactly the floor, all on Legs A; 1 done a week because the machine was skipped at Chennai on 14 October. Last 60 lb for 15, 15 at Singapore on 5 October. Tonight is the read.

calves.why: Six direct sets a rotation (calf press 3 on Legs A, 3 on Legs B), exactly the floor of 6; the 9 on paper adds half a set from each of the six leg-curl sets. If the calf press slot went without a replacement, direct calf work would be zero, so it will not go without one. 2.6 a week done: no calf press since Singapore on 5 October (290 for 15, 12, then 270 for 14), skipped at Chennai on 14 October, and no leg night since. The read that was to decide this slot, a Legs A at Vancouver on 25 October, did not happen, so it is re-dated: tonight carries two deload sets at 230 (80% of the 290 top set is 232), and the 2 November review keeps the slot if Vancouver can load it or gives calves a slot this gym has.

Eight planned (cable crunch 3 and 3, and from 26 October the ab wheel rollout 2 in place of the hanging leg raise), 2 done a week because both leg days have been missed or cut. The rotation: the leg raise's second set slipped from 12 to 10 on 17 September and 5 October with no weight to add, and every other ab set is a crunch, so the rollout adds an anti-extension lift. The 14 October crunches were typed in on 15 October within two seconds, so remembered.

The hold stands on the rebuild itself, 235 for 5, 5, 5 against the sick 225 night, not on a pass that was never tested; all four sets at 235 for 5 after the deload is what moves it. hip-abductor.why: Not logged since 60 lb for 15, 15 at Singapore on 5 October. Tonight 45 for 12, one set, on the Vancouver machine; first set finds it.

findings.finding: The review stated deload numbers for lifts on sessions that carried no override, and the app's own deload card would have shown a different weight on every one of them (smith incline press 105 against the review's 130; shoulder press 35 against 45; wide pulldown 82.5 and 90 against 95; face pulls 15 and 20 against 17.5; dumbbell lateral raise 10 against 12.5; close pulldown 97.5 against 100; dumbbell and incline curls 20 against 22.5), because the engine skips nights logged under a different movement name and rounds to its own grid.
findings.why: Overrides are now written for every loaded slot of all six sessions, in pounds, each earned from the last same-movement night on the gym it was logged at, and the packet drives those cards through 31 October while nothing new has synced. Every lift why now states the number its card shows, and the brief and block say the other five sessions carry numbers on this packet. The one slot with no log at all, the Push A machine lateral raise, carries 30 and its card says that is a starting guess, not a number from the log.
